title: Rigetti Computing Finalizes Definitive $100 Million CHIPS Act Award with U.S. Department of Commerce - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Rigetti Computing Finalizes Definitive $100 Million CHIPS Act Award with U.S. Department of Commerce

Superconducting hardware developer Rigetti Computing, Inc. (NASDAQ: RGTI) has executed a definitive agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce for a $100 million federal R&D award under the CHIPS and Science Act. Issued through the CHIPS Research and Development Office, the capital deployment converts the previously announced Letter of Intent (LOI) into a formal contract to resolve physical scaling bottlenecks in superconducting quantum processors.

The contract structures funding across three engineering projects: compressing and miniaturizing high-density readout control electronics, engineering a multi-stage cryostat architecture to expand dilution refrigeration capacity, and advancing in-house fabrication capabilities at Rigetti’s Fab-1 facility to manufacture high-connectivity multi-chiplet QPU architectures. As a condition of the award, the Department of Commerce will receive a minority, non-controlling equity stake in Rigetti.

[ Rigetti CHIPS Act $100M Award & Technical Scope ]Award StructureEngineering Project TrackSystem & Fab Integration• Total Value: $100 Million• Miniature Readout Electronics• Integrated On-Chip Signal Processing• Program: CHIPS R&D Office BAA• High-Capacity Cryostat Architecture• Multi-Order Expansion of Cryo Cooling• Consideration: Govt Minority Equity• Advanced Chiplet Fabrication• Fab-1 High-Connectivity QPU Scaling

The funding supports Rigetti’s chiplet-based hardware roadmap. Building on its 108-qubit Cepheus-1-108Q system (composed of twelve 9-qubit chiplets) and its on-premises Novera QPU offerings, the agreement provides capital to scale production of multi-chiplet architectures with 50-70 nanosecond gate speeds for defense, national laboratory, and commercial cloud deployments.
